# Vendored converter provenance

The offline decoder subset in this directory is based on [`HRuiCcc/music-geshizhuanhuan`](https://github.com/HRuiCcc/music-geshizhuanhuan), pinned to commit `28f4ed0724f85978405d961c0e955266eed383ee` (2026-09-02). The upstream repository archive for that commit was checked against SHA-256 `6B837A2F522048391A94E1E2861B460276FB1C6D9A2A5CD4EB2A192C8D1F9654`.

The decoder code is MIT-licensed; the complete upstream MIT text is in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). This project vendors only the NCM, QMC, and KGM/VPR decoder modules, their shared cipher/error/model code, and the bundled public KGM key asset. The third-party GUI, CLI, downloader/network code, KWM support, local EKey database, tests, and client integration are excluded.

Local changes restrict the helper to offline decoding, remove EKey database and user-supplied key paths, identify decoder families from file bytes, and return `KeyUnavailable` for QMC v2 variants without an embedded key. KGM/VPR crypto versions are deliberately limited to v3/v4. These changes do not establish compatibility with every platform build; see [`../../docs/ENCRYPTED_FORMAT_SUPPORT.md`](../../docs/ENCRYPTED_FORMAT_SUPPORT.md) for sample status and limits.

The helper is built as an x64 onedir executable with CPython 3.14.3, PyInstaller 6.22.3, and PyCryptodome 3.20.0. The bundled CPython runtime also includes OpenSSL 3.0.18 libraries (`libcrypto-3.dll` SHA-256 `E03DD02FDCFB791981C9962827CFCF495F2A47A514C1526EFB57F847A9DF514A`; `libssl-3.dll` SHA-256 `1E4BC0638682BFCBB36F4465D6A2E9944D917A60F05ECC8DDF9E96847E05E13F`), under Apache License 2.0; the complete license text is included in [`../../licenses/MusicConverter-NOTICES.txt`](../../licenses/MusicConverter-NOTICES.txt). See the [OpenSSL source](https://github.com/openssl/openssl) and [license](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/openssl-3.0/LICENSE.txt). The application extracts that archive into a GUID-scoped task directory under `AppPaths.SettingsDirectory`, runs it without a shell, and deletes only that task directory after completion or cancellation. No Python installation is required on the user's machine.
